official.description_text:
Researcher in power electronics and EV charging infrastructure
Apply for position
KTH Royal Institute of Technology, School of Electrical Engineering and Computer Science
Job description
The electrification of heavy-duty transportation requires next-generation charging infrastructure capable of delivering fast, efficient, and reliable charging.
This project focuses on the design, modeling, control, and hardware development of fast charging systems for heavy-duty electric vehicles. The research covers high-power power electronic converters, system-level modeling, control strategies, grid integration, the coordination of mobile energy storage.
This project is funded by Sweden's Innovation Agency, in collaboration with City of Stockholm, Hitachi Energy, Vattenfall, etc.
Qualifications
Requirements
A doctoral degree or an equivalent foreign degree
Strong expertise in at least one of the following topics: power electronics hardware, EV charging converter design, or EV charging management
Knowledge of diversity and equal opportunity issues, with specific focus on gender equality
Research expertise in power electronics or power system
Collaborative abilities
Independence
Preferred qualifications
Experience with hardware development
Strong publication records in top IEEE Transactions
Strong self-motivation in research
Great emphasis will be placed on personal skills.
Join us at KTH
KTH shapes the future through education, research and innovation. As a leading international technical university, we play an active role in advancing the transition towards a sustainable society. At KTH, you have the opportunity to grow and develop in a creative and dynamic environment, with good working conditions and attractive benefits. Equality, diversity and equal opportunities are essential to quality and form an integral part of KTH’s core values as a university and public authority.
Learn more about our benefits and what it's like to work and grow at KTH
.

To apply for the position
Log into KTH's recruitment system in order to apply for this position. You are responsible to ensure that your application is complete according to the instructions in the ad.
The application must include:
CV including relevant professional experience and knowledge.
Copy of diplomas and grades from your previous university studies. Translations into English or Swedish if the original documents have not been issued in any of these languages.
Research statement about your previous research achievement (2 pages) and your research plan (2-3 pages).
Your complete application must be received by KTH no later than the last day of application, midnight CET/CEST (Central European Time/Central European Summer Time).
About the employment
The employment is valid for a limited time according to the agreement - for up to 12 months, with access according to agreement.

In such cases, a prerequisite for employment is that the applicant is approved following the security clearance.

ai.summary: Research position at KTH focusing on design, modeling, control, and hardware development of fast charging systems for heavy-duty electric vehicles. Work covers high-power power electronic converters, system-level modeling, control strategies, grid integration, and mobile energy storage coordination. Funded by Sweden's Innovation Agency in collaboration with industry partners.

thematic_fit.rationale: No thematic alignment. The posting is pure power electronics and EV charging infrastructure engineering. No mention of immersive systems, human-centred design, learning, collaboration, spatial cognition, or XR. Researcher's domains (human-centred XR, collaborative immersive systems, spatial learning, wayfinding) are entirely orthogonal to power system hardware and control.

methodological_fit.rationale: Minimal methodological fit. The posting emphasizes hardware development, converter design, modeling, and control strategies—all at the systems/electrical engineering level. Researcher has no expertise in power electronics, control engineering, or hardware development. The position requires 'strong expertise in at least one of: power electronics hardware, EV charging converter design, or EV charging management.' Researcher has none of these.

growth_value.rationale: Essentially no growth value for target identity. This role develops expertise in power electronics and EV infrastructure, which are in the excluded directions (pure technical engineering). Does not advance human-centred XR, spatial cognition, immersive systems, or HCI research.

strategic_value.rationale: KTH is a strong institution in Stockholm, Sweden (preferred country/region). Funding is secure (12 months, industry-backed). However, the research mission (power electronics, EV charging hardware) has no alignment with human-centred immersive systems or HCI. No research community fit. Position does not support pathway to target identity.

EV charging infrastructure and management systems
eligibility_flags: Requires PhD; researcher holds MSc by Research (in progress). Must be conferred before employment decision.
Position title is 'Researcher' (not postdoc), and duration is 'up to 12 months' with flexible start. Employment status ambiguous.
Security clearance mentioned (Protective Security Act 2018:585). Applicability and timing unknown.
risks: Severe domain mismatch: power electronics and EV charging hardware vs. human-centred immersive systems research. Fundamentally different research culture, methodology, and tools.
Researcher has no background in power systems, hardware development, or electrical engineering at the required level. Skill gap is very large.
Position explicitly targets 'strong publication records in top IEEE Transactions' and 'hardware development expertise.' Researcher's publication track record is in HCI/XR, not power electronics.
Taking this role would derail PhD trajectory in target research direction and require retraining in an excluded technical domain (power systems engineering).
No research community overlap. KTH's School of Electrical Engineering has no documented HCI, XR, or immersive systems research. Career development within target identity would be blocked.
Industry collaborators (Hitachi Energy, Vattenfall) are utilities/hardware vendors, not immersive systems or human factors research partners.
